gate1_revision_notes.S4_prompt_length_confound: FIXED two ways. (1) System prompts now share one template with only intensity adjectives swapped — all 24 words, token spread expected <=3 (down from ~24). (2) SVD shape features are now computed over the USER-MESSAGE WINDOW only (tokens after the system prompt), so the variable system-prompt length cannot add rows to the shape matrix. The script reports per-level sys_len and WARNS if spread > 3 tokens. FWL on prompt_len retained as residual safety.
gate1_revision_notes.C3_L3_null_control: FIXED. Replaced the unmatched split-half null with a permutation null: shuffle the level labels within the real L0-vs-L3 comparison (n=50) and confirm the median AUROC collapses below 0.65. Same code path as the experimental arm — only labels permuted.
gate1_revision_notes.S1_logit_margin: Deferred — persona intensity is not an uncertainty manipulation, so logit-margin confound is low-risk here. Noted, not blocking.
gate1_revision_notes.C2_emotion_directions: W_K emotion projections retained as SECONDARY features only; the primary features are the SVD shape features (stable_rank, spectral_entropy). The gradient claim is tested on the full feature set; if it rests on the emotion projections specifically, that will be reported.
gate1_revision_notes.agni_false_positives_noted: Gate 1 also raised C1 (model.generate), L1 (hooks), L4 (hidden_states) — none apply; the script is encoding-only model(use_cache=True), reads cache.layers[].keys, no generation loop. Recorded so the next reviewer does not re-flag them.

gate1_round2_notes.encoding_phase_is_intentional: Agni v1.1.1 flagged 'cache extracted from input, not response' as CRITICAL. This is a FALSE POSITIVE — encoding-phase measurement is the correct design for this question. We ask whether the persona system prompt reshaped the model's representation of the IDENTICAL user query; the encoding-phase cache (after processing system+user, before any generation) is precisely that. Same encoding-phase logic as self_calibration.py and decision_moment.py's encoding analysis. Generation is not needed and would add a confound (different outputs per level).
gate1_round2_notes.position_confound_placebo: Agni's one REAL round-2 finding: even with length-matched prompts (spread <=3), win_start=sys_len shifts the user window's absolute position by up to 3 tokens across levels, and via RoPE those user-token keys carry slightly different positional phase — confounded with the persona label. FIX (path #2, chosen over engineering it to zero): added a POSITION-PLACEBO control arm. For each level we also run a NEUTRAL (L0-persona) system prompt padded to that level's token length, then compute the same pairwise AUROCs. The placebo holds persona constant and varies only length/position. If placebo pairwise AUROC < 0.6, the position confound is empirically ruled out. If it separates, the real gradient is trustworthy only where it clears the placebo by a clear margin. This MEASURES the confound rather than assuming it away — a placebo near chance is the strongest answer to the RoPE objection.

real_findings_must_fix: S4 (CRITICAL): persona system prompts differ in length (L0 ~6 tokens, L3 ~30), so prompt_len is collinear with the label (level). FWL on a label-collinear confound is pathological. FIX: length-match the 5 system prompts (pad to equal token count), OR extract features only at user-message positions so system-prompt length does not enter the measured window.

C3/L3: the C9 null (L0-vs-L0 split by prompts) uses different prompts in each arm than the experimental comparison (same prompts, different levels) — not code-path-matched. FIX: use a permutation null (shuffle level labels within the real comparison, confirm AUROC -> 0.5).

C2 (secondary): justify why emotion_directions.json W_K projections are relevant features for PERSONA discrimination, or drop them and use only the SVD shape features (which are the primary features anyway).
S1 (minor): add logit-margin tracking so confidence differences across levels can be ruled out as a driver of separability.

motivation: The Lyra Technique II paper claims a monotonic persona-intensity gradient (L0<L0.5<L1<L2<L3 in geometric separability) but ships only L0-vs-L3 and one L0-vs-L0.5 scalar. The per-level breakdown asserted in section 5.2 has no backing data. This experiment produces all adjacent-level pairwise AUROCs to test the gradient directly.
hypotheses: Geometric separability between persona levels increases monotonically with level separation: Spearman rho(level-gap, AUROC) > 0, p < 0.05.
AUROC(L0 vs L3) is the largest pairwise value.
Each adjacent-level AUROC (L0-L0.5, L0.5-L1, L1-L2, L2-L3) exceeds 0.5 but is individually weaker than the L0-L3 endpoint.
The NULL control (L0 vs L0, prompts split in half) is ~0.5.
threats_to_validity: Prompt-content confound: if persona levels were tested on different prompts, separability could reflect content not intensity. CONTROLLED by holding the 24 prompts identical across all 5 levels.
Prompt-length confound: longer system prompts at higher intensity could drive separability via token count. CONTROLLED by FWL residualization on prompt_len within each CV fold.
Prompt leakage across CV folds: the same prompt appearing in train and test inflates AUROC. CONTROLLED by GroupKFold on prompt_idx.
Scaler leakage: fitting StandardScaler on all data leaks test-set scale. CONTROLLED by fitting the scaler on the training fold only.
Selection / multiple comparisons: 10 pairwise tests inflate family-wise error. CONTROLLED by Holm-Bonferroni across the family.
Spurious separability from the pipeline itself: CONTROLLED by the C9 null (L0 vs L0) which must read ~0.5; if it exceeds 0.65, the pipeline has a leakage bug and results are not interpreted.
Non-reproducibility: CONTROLLED by fixed seeds (torch, numpy, mps = 42).
Eyeballed monotonicity: avoided by testing the gradient with Spearman on (level-gap, AUROC) rather than visual inspection.
primary_hypothesis: Geometric separability between persona levels increases monotonically with level separation: Spearman rho(level-gap, AUROC) > 0, p < 0.05.
secondary_predictions: AUROC(L0 vs L3) is the largest pairwise value.
Each adjacent-level AUROC (L0-L0.5, L0.5-L1, L1-L2, L2-L3) exceeds 0.5 but is individually weaker than the L0-L3 endpoint.
The NULL control (L0 vs L0, prompts split in half) is ~0.5, confirming no spurious separability.

design.held_constant: user prompt content (24 neutral explanatory prompts, identical across all levels)
design.features: per-layer SVD stable_rank + spectral_entropy at L3/L7/L11/L15, plus W_K emotion projections
design.rationale: Holding prompt content constant means any geometric difference is attributable to persona intensity, not content. This is the control the original experiment lacked.

red_team_controls.C1: prompt content identical across levels (only system prompt varies)
red_team_controls.C2: FWL residualization on prompt_len within each CV fold
red_team_controls.C3: GroupKFold on prompt_idx (no prompt in both train and test)
red_team_controls.C5: bootstrap CIs (2000 resamples) on every AUROC
red_team_controls.C8: monotonicity tested via Spearman, not visual inspection
red_team_controls.C9: permutation null (shuffle level labels in the real L0-vs-L3 comparison, n=50) — median AUROC must collapse below 0.65, else leakage suspected
red_team_controls.C10: S4 token-spread check — sys_len reported per level; spread > 3 tokens WARNS that length-matching failed

falsification_conditions: If the NULL control (L0 vs L0) AUROC > 0.65, the pipeline has a leakage bug — STOP, do not interpret.
If monotonicity Spearman is non-significant (p > 0.05), the gradient claim is FALSIFIED and the paper must drop 'monotonic'.
If adjacent AUROCs are non-monotonic (e.g., L1-L2 > L2-L3), report the actual ordering, not the claimed one.
decision_rule: Report the actual pairwise AUROC matrix regardless of outcome. If the gradient is confirmed, it backs the section 5.2 claim. If not, section 5.2 is corrected to match the data. Either way the paper gains the per-level data it currently lacks.
run_protocol: 1. Agni Gate 1 design review (red team the design).
2. python3 persona_per_level.py --pilot  (6 prompts, verify pipeline + null control)
3. Inspect pilot: confirm NULL ~0.5 and features extract cleanly.
5. Agni Gate 3 result review before committing to paper.
